newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up 1.01 pct on minister comments.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up 1.01 pct on minister comments.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Thursday after Finance Minister Paul Chiu said on Wednesday that his ministry would not pressure the stock market in a new crackdown on manipulation, brokers said.
Brokers said Wall Street's overnight rebound and Thursday announcement by South Korea's Samsung to cut production of 16 megabit dynamic random access memory chips helped the gain.
The index ended up 72.44 points or 1.01 percent at 7,221.98. Turnover was a heavy T$81.4 billion.
"Minister Chiu's comments helped ease worries on more stock market crackdowns," said Nomura Securities analyst Ben Lee.
Electronics led the gains, rising 1.99 percent, in a reaction to IBM shares' overnight rise in the United States.

Samsung's DRAM production cut also helped some DRAM-linked shares, with Acer up 50 cents to T$51 and Taiwan Semiconductor up 50 cents to T$56.5. Both shares have affiliates -- unlisted TI-Acer and Vanguard -- producing 16 megabit DRAMs.
Brokers said Samsung's move would help DRAM price rebounds.
"Samsung's move should help a short-term price rebound for 16 megabit DRAMs -- good news for local DRAM makers," Lee said.
However, a major price recovery in semiconductors was not expected until the third quarter, brokers said.
"We expect the semiconductor industry to start recovery in the third quarter," said Michael Hung of Nikko Securities. He said it would be a good time to buy the sector in May or June.
Machinery and textile shares were also strong.
Brokers noted rising buying on hopes that the shares would rise before the seven-day Chinese New Year holiday begins on February 4.

"Those who don't want to hold shares in the upcoming holiday have almost finished selling last week, now those who expect a Lunar New Year rally start to enter," said Lee of Nomura. A 7,200-7,300 range was seen for Friday.
